==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|mēn|a=RP,AU,NZ}}, {{IPA|en|/miːn/}} * {{IPA|en|/miːn/|/mijən/|a=Local Dublin}} * {{IPA|en|/min/|a=GA,CA}} * {{audio|en|en-us-mean.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|iːn|s=1}} * {{hmp|en|mene|mien|mesne}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|menen||to intend; remember; lament; comfort}}, from {{inh|en|ang|mǣnan||to mean, complain}}, {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*mainijan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*mainijaną||to mean, think; complain}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*meyn-||to think}}, or perhaps from {{der|en|ine-pro|*meyno-}}, extended form of {{der|en|ine-pro|*mey-}}. Germanic cognates include {{cog|fy|miene||to deem, think}} ({{cog|ofs|mēna||to signify}}), {{cog|nl|menen||to believe, think, mean}} ({{cog|dum|menen||to think, intend}}), {{cog|de|meinen||to think, mean, believe}}, {{cog|osx|mēnian}}. Indo-European cognates include {{cog|sga|mían||wish, desire}} and {{cog|pl|mienić||to signify, believe}}. Non-Indo-European cognates include {{cog|fi|mainita||to mention}}, {{cog|fi|meinata||to mean, to plan, to intend}} {{cog|et|mainima||to mention}}, {{cog|se|máinnastit||to tell}}. Related to {{m|en|moan}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|~t}} # To intend. ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[intend]], to [[plan]] (to do); to have as one's intention. {{defdate|from 8th c.}} ##: {{syn|en|intend}} ##: {{ux|en|I didn't '''mean''' to knock your tooth out.}} ##: {{ux|en|I '''mean''' to go to Arévalo in Spain this summer; I’ve been '''meaning''' to tell you for weeks, but I’ve just found the time.}} ##: {{ux|en|I '''meant''' to take the car in for a smog check, but it slipped my mind.}} ##: {{ux|en|The authors '''meant''' a challenge to the status quo.}} ##: {{ux|en|Do you '''mean''' to say you regret it after all?}} ##* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|1|iii|48|Doo not my captaines and my ſouldiers looke
As if they '''meant''' to conquer ''Affrica''?}} ## {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have as intentions of a given kind. {{defdate|from 14th c.}} ##: {{ux|en|Don't be angry; she '''meant''' well.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|usually in passive}} To [[intend]] (something) for a given purpose or fate; to [[predestine]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}} ##: {{ux|en|Actually this desk was '''meant''' for the subeditor.}} ##: {{ux|en|Man was not '''meant''' to question such things.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[intend]] an ensuing comment or statement as an explanation. ##: {{ux|en|Your reasoning seems needlessly abstruse, complex, and verbose for me. I '''mean''', could you dumb it down for my sake?}} # To convey (a meaning). ## {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[convey]] (a given sense); to [[signify]], or [[indicate]] (an object or idea). {{defdate|from 8th c.}} ##: {{syn|en|convey|indicate|signify}} ##: {{ux|en|The sky is red this morning—does that '''mean''' we're in for a storm?}} ##* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|title=A better waterworks|issue=8838|url=https://www.economist.com/technology-quarterly/2013/06/01/a-better-waterworks|page=5|passage=An artificial kidney these days still '''means''' a refrigerator-sized dialysis machine. Such devices mimic the way real kidneys cleanse blood and eject impurities and surplus water as urine.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250422080456/https://www.economist.com/technology-quarterly/2013/06/01/a-better-waterworks|archivedate=22 April 2025}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} Of a word, symbol etc: to have reference to, to [[signify]]. {{defdate|from 8th c.}} ##: {{ux|en|What does this hieroglyph '''mean'''?}} ##* {{RQ:Guardian|date=2024-6-20|author=Eva Corlett|title=Fidlets, fingies and riding a doo: study sheds light on Antarctic English slang|url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/20/fidlets-fingies-and-riding-a-doo-antarctica-english-slang-terms|passage=Americans, for example, call newcomers to Antarctica “fingies”, which comes from FNGs – a borrowed military abbreviation that '''means''' “Fucking New Guy”.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013073203/https://www.theguardian.com/world/article/2024/jun/20/fidlets-fingies-and-riding-a-doo-antarctica-english-slang-terms|archivedate=13 October 2026}} ## {{lb|en|transitive}} Of a person (or animal etc): to intend to [[express]], to [[imply]], to [[hint]] at, to [[allude]]. ##: {{syn|en|hint|imply}} ##: {{syn|en|get at}} ##: {{ux|en|I’m afraid I don’t understand what you '''mean'''.}} ##: {{ux|en|He’s a little different, if you know what I '''mean'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To have [[conviction]] in (something said or expressed); to be sincere in (what one says). {{defdate|from 18th c.}} #: {{ux|en|Does she really '''mean''' what she said to him last night?}} #: {{ux|en|Say what you mean and '''mean''' what you say.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[cause]] or [[produce]] (a given [[result]]); to [[bring about]] (a given result). {{defdate|from 19th c.}} #: {{syn|en|bring about|cause|lead to|result in}} #: {{ux|en|One faltering step '''means''' certain death.}} #: {{ux|en|This breakthrough will '''mean''' that we spend less on electricity bills.}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2014-06-14|volume=411|issue=8891|title=It’s a gas|url=https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2014/06/14/its-a-gas|passage=One of the hidden glories of Victorian engineering is proper drains.{{...}}But out of sight is out of mind. And that, together with the inherent yuckiness of the subject, '''means''' that many old sewers have been neglected and are in dire need of repair.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250531141405/https://www.economist.com/science-and-technology/2014/06/14/its-a-gas|archivedate=31 May 2025}} # {{lb|en|usually with ''to''}} To be of some level of importance. #: {{ux|en|That little dog '''meant''' everything to me.}} #: {{ux|en|Formality and titles '''mean''' nothing in their circle.}} # {{lb|en|Ireland|UK|_|regional}} To
